title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 14
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: A churn holds 40 litres of milk. 8 litres are drawn off and replaced with water; the same is done a second time. How much milk remains?
questions.explanation: Each round leaves 32/40 of whatever milk was there, so after two rounds 40 × (0.8)² = 25.6 litres remain. Taking 8 litres away twice gives 24 litres, which would be right only if pure milk were removed the second time — but by then the churn is already part water.

questions.prompt: £6,000.00 grows by 10% in its first year and 40% in its second, each added to the balance. What is it worth after two years?
questions.explanation: After one year the fund holds £6,600.00, and 40% of that is £2,640.00, giving £9,240.00. Adding the two rates to make 50% of the original gives £9,000.00 and misses the second year's growth on the first year's gain.

questions.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 162 degrees. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle is 180 − 162 = 18 degrees, and the exterior angles of any polygon add to 360, so there are 360 / 18 = 20 of them — and so 20 sides. 18 is the exterior angle itself, not a count of sides.

questions.prompt: Taking pi as 22/7, a circle is drawn inside a square of side 14 cm, touching all four sides. What area of the square lies outside the circle?
questions.explanation: The square measures 196 cm² and the circle has radius 7 cm, so its area is 22/7 × 7² = 154 cm². The difference is 42 cm². 154 cm² is the circle itself, which is much the larger part of the square.

questions.prompt: A class of 50 contains 20 girls. The boys average 64 marks and the girls average 76. What is the class average?
questions.explanation: There are 50 − 20 = 30 boys, scoring 1,920 marks between them, and the girls score 1,520. That is 3,440 marks over 50 pupils: 68.8. Averaging the two group means gives 70 and treats the two groups as the same size.

questions.prompt: A fair six-sided die is rolled and shows an even number. What is the probability that it is a 6?
questions.explanation: Knowing the result is even narrows the possibilities to 2, 4 and 6 — three outcomes, all equally likely. One of them is a 6, so the probability is 1/3. 1/6 is the chance of rolling a 6 before anything is known about the result.

questions.prompt: Solve for x: 3(2x − 5) = 4(x + 2)
questions.explanation: Expanding both sides gives 6x − 15 = 4x + 8. Taking 4x from each side leaves 2x − 15 = 8, and adding 15 gives 2x = 23, so x = 11.5. Subtracting 15 rather than adding it gives -3.5, the commonest slip when the constant is moved the wrong way.

questions.prompt: 6 workers take 8 days to complete half a job. How long do 10 workers take to finish the other half?
questions.explanation: Half the job is 6 × 8 = 48 worker-days, and the remaining half is the same again. Shared between 10 workers that is 4.8 days. Halving as well as rescaling gives 2.4 days and forgets that 48 worker-days is only half the work.

questions.prompt: An item costs £63.00. At what price must it sell for the profit to be 30% of the selling price?
questions.explanation: If profit is 30% of the price, cost is the other 70%, so the price is £63.00 / 0.7 = £90.00 and the profit £27.00. Adding 30% to the cost gives £81.90, where the profit is 30% of cost but only 23.08% of the selling price.

questions.prompt: What is 0.27 recurring, with the 27 repeating for ever, as a fraction in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: Let x be the number. Then 100x = 27.2727…, and subtracting gives 99x = 27, so x = 27/99. Both parts divide by 9, leaving 3/11. 27/99 is correct but not in its simplest form, and 27/100 is the terminating decimal 0.27, which is a different number.

questions.prompt: What is the length of the longest straight line that fits inside a box measuring 6 cm by 8 cm by 24 cm?
questions.explanation: The space diagonal is the square root of 6² + 8² + 24² = 36 + 64 + 576 = 676, which is 26 cm. Adding the three edges gives 38 cm, a route along the box rather than through it.

questions.prompt: A task begins at 14:45 and takes 3 hours 50 minutes. At what time does it finish?
questions.explanation: 45 minutes past 14 plus 50 minutes is 95 minutes, which is one hour and 35 minutes. So the finish is 14 + 3 + 1 = 18 hours and 35 minutes: 18:35. Carrying the minutes without converting to an hour gives 18:95, which is not a time.

questions.prompt: A photograph 15 cm by 10 cm is enlarged so that the longer side becomes 24 cm. What is the new shorter side?
questions.explanation: The longer side is multiplied by 24/15 = 1.6, and an enlargement multiplies both sides by the same factor: 10 × 1.6 = 16 cm. Adding the 9 cm that the long side gained gives 19 cm and would change the shape of the photograph.

questions.prompt: A price of £234.00 includes VAT at 20%. How much of it is VAT?
questions.explanation: The gross figure is 120% of the price before tax, so the net price is £234.00 / 1.2 = £195.00, and the VAT is the remaining £39.00. Taking 20% of the gross gives £46.80, which charges the tax on the tax as well.

questions.prompt: What is the mean of the first 12 multiples of 5?
questions.explanation: The multiples run from 5 to 60, evenly spaced, so their mean is the average of the first and last: (5 + 60) / 2 = 32.5. 60 is the largest of them, not the average.

questions.prompt: A taxi charges £3.20 plus £1.45 a kilometre. What is the greatest whole number of kilometres that £20.00 will cover?
questions.explanation: After the £3.20 flag fall, £16.80 is left, which buys £16.80 / £1.45 = 11.59 km — 11 whole kilometres, costing £19.15. Ignoring the flag fall gives 13 km, which would cost £22.05, over budget.

questions.prompt: At what value of x does the line 4x + 5y = 60 cross the x-axis?
questions.explanation: On the x-axis y is zero, so the equation becomes 4x = 60 and x = 15. 12 is where the line crosses the y-axis, found by setting x to zero instead.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest number greater than 3 that leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 4, 5 and 6?
questions.explanation: A number leaving the same remainder 3 with all three divisors is 3 more than a common multiple of them. The lowest common multiple of 4, 5, 6 is 60, so the number is 60 + 3 = 63. 60 itself divides exactly by all three and leaves no remainder at all.

questions.prompt: 40 litres are bought at £1.52 a litre and 25 litres at £1.61 a litre. What is the average price paid per litre?
questions.explanation: The two purchases cost £60.80 and £40.25, a total of £101.05 for 65 litres: £1.55 a litre. Averaging the two prices gives £1.57 and ignores that more was bought at the cheaper price.

questions.prompt: A triangle has an area of 84 cm² and a base of 24 cm. What is the perpendicular height to that base?
questions.explanation: Area is half the base times the height, so 84 = 24 × h / 2 and h = 2 × 84 / 24 = 7 cm. Dividing the area by the base without doubling gives 3.5 cm and forgets the half in the formula.

questions.prompt: £7,500.00 earns £1,350.00 in simple interest over 3 years. What is the annual rate?
questions.explanation: Simple interest is capital × rate × years, so the rate is £1,350.00 / (£7,500.00 × 3) = 6% a year. Dividing by the capital alone gives 18%, which is the total return over all 3 years rather than the annual rate.
